chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fadhdhal, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Buraid ibn Mu'awiya al-'Ijli, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Eat from the hunt that which was killed by the sword, the arrow, and the spear.
And he was asked about game that was hunted and then the people divided it among themselves before it died; so he said: There is no problem with it.

key_terms.الرُّمح: al-rumh — the spear; a piercing weapon
key_terms.السَّهم: al-sahm — the arrow; a projectile weapon
key_terms.السَّيف: al-sayf — the sword; a bladed weapon
key_terms.الصَّيْد: al-sayd — hunted game; encompasses both the act of hunting and the animal hunted
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: la ba'sa bihi — 'there is no problem/harm in it'; standard juristic formula permitting something

ai.seo_question: What weapons make hunted game permissible to eat according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) issues two related rulings on hunting: first, that game is permissible to eat if killed by edged weapons (sword, arrow, or spear); second, that game which is divided among hunters before it dies is still permissible. These rulings were given in the context of 7th-century Arabian hunting practices, addressing concerns about whether divided game that had not yet completed dying was still lawful. The permissibility hinged on the lethal nature of the weapon used, not on the animal's final moment of death.
